title: 14-year-old with brief, frequent attacks of incoordination triggered by sudden movement

provenance.citation: Synthetic case drafted 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: "When I suddenly start running or get startled, my legs and hands go wobbly for a minute."
history_of_present_illness: Since age 9, brief attacks lasting 30 seconds to 3 minutes of limb incoordination, unsteadiness and slurred speech, several times per day on some days. Triggered by sudden movement (standing up quickly, starting a sprint), startle, and emotional upset. Sometimes she feels the muscles of her hands and around her eyes 'ripple' between attacks. No loss of consciousness. Normal between attacks except for occasional muscle stiffness.

movement_findings.observation: Attack provoked in clinic by rising quickly: 90-second episode of limb ataxia and dysarthria; no dystonic or choreic postures.
Interictal: fine continuous rippling of periorbital muscles and small hand muscles, consistent with myokymia.

family_history: Father had similar 'wobbly spells' as a teenager that diminished in adulthood.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Pediatrician raised paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia because of movement triggering.
